<description>
I agree the O(n²) cost of reading a whole witness with `btck_witness_stack_get_item_at` needs fixing. I'm less sure a new callback type is the best way to do it which #36909 is doing. Instead we could expose the witness's serialized bytes and let the bindings or caller decide how to decode them, this also follows the `*_to_bytes` functions we already have in the API.
</description>

[2026-11-19] c:7019018519 comment by pzafonte (contributor):
Yuvicc, thanks for putting this up. It looks like it comes down to where the items are decoded. `btck_witness_stack_get_items` decodes them in the kernel and returns pointers that are valid for the duration of the existence of the witness stack and `btck_witness_stack_to_bytes` returns the serialization and each binding would decode the items themselves.

What I'm trying to accomplish is to make an efficient form of the design that the API already has (`btck_witness_stack_get_item_at`) and to decode once in the kernel so that consumers don't need to reimplement consensus parsing.
</new_statements>
